about.title: Willows Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Willows is a small place. With about 6,069 residents, a sudden death here is rarely anonymous; neighbors, coworkers and classmates feel it too. Public collision records for 2025 list a single injury crash in the city and no traffic deaths, which means a fatal loss stands out all the more when it happens, whether on Interstate 5 Northbound, along W Wood Street or Sycamore Street, or out on Rt 162. Fatal harm is not limited to the road, either. A workplace incident on a Glenn County farm, a medication mistake, or neglect in a care setting can leave a family facing the same emptiness. California law allows a spouse or domestic partner and children, and in some cases other dependents or heirs, to bring a civil wrongful death claim. That claim is separate from anything a prosecutor may do, and it generally must be filed within two years of the date of death. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Willows families with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so there is nothing to pay unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Willows Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California gives a spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs following. An attorney can sort out your family's standing before anything is filed.

items.title: The clock is watched for you
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county or state agency is involved. Early contact protects that deadline.

items.title: Every kind of loss counted
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the love, companionship and guidance your family has lost. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so no fee is owed unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My spouse died in a crash on Interstate 5 near Willows. Does it matter that we live somewhere else?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim in California is generally tied to where the death occurred and who was responsible, not to where the surviving family lives. The crash happened in Glenn County, so the claim can proceed here even if you are out of the area. An independent attorney can handle most of the process without you having to travel back and forth.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: You do not. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that runs on its own track, separate from any criminal case brought by the district attorney. The two can move forward at the same time, and the outcome of one does not decide the other. Waiting can be risky, because the two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless of the criminal court schedule.

items.question: What if the crash involved a Glenn County road crew or another government agency?
items.answer: Claims against a public entity in California follow a different and much shorter timeline than the standard two years, and a formal claim usually must be presented to the agency first. Missing that early step can close the door on the case entirely. If there is any chance a city, county or state agency played a role, it is worth speaking with an attorney right away.
